stories.headline: A Bootprint Found at the Edge of the Drive: Single, Partial, Facing the Jeep; the Bandit Has Been Here
stories.byline: By our Trail Correspondent, filing from the front drive
body: At some point between the last light of Wednesday and the first light of Thursday, a boot touched the gravel of the front drive — left foot, partial heel-to-arch impression, facing the passenger-side mirror where the orange duck stands. The print is clean: no smear, no scuff, no sign of hurry. Whoever made it stopped, observed, and departed without event. The measurement places the print's owner at approximately five feet ten, though the subcommittee has noted, correctly, that gravel is not a controlled surface and they should not be held to that.

The two ducks are undisturbed. The angle between them — forty-seven degrees, orange to original, passenger to driver — remains as it was. The orange duck has not moved. The original duck has not moved. The bootprint is ten inches from the passenger-side tyre, which places its maker well inside the range at which the numeral 7 would have been legible, if you knew to look for it. Lucy was not asleep. No one is prepared to explain why she did not bark.

stories.headline: Thursday Clears Its Throat; Christine Answers; Four Accounts Are Resolved Before the Vaults Have Finished Warming Up
body: The bank opened at nine. By nine forty-three, the overnight disputes had been catalogued, prioritised, and reduced from four to one — the remaining case involving a contested inheritance across three goblin sub-jurisdictions, which is not a problem so much as a diplomatic situation, and diplomatic situations are precisely what Christine is for.

Griphook the Younger has begun arriving three minutes early on Thursdays specifically. He has not explained this. He does not need to. The goblins keep their own counsel, but they are not subtle about the ones they trust to keep theirs.

stories.headline: Lucy Did Not Bark: Full Statement Issued; Statement Raises More Questions Than It Answers; a Follow-Up Statement Is Expected
body: Lucy, Senior Familiar and Household Intelligence Officer, has released a formal statement regarding her conduct during the presumed window of the bootprint's arrival. The statement reads, in its entirety: 'Insufficient grounds for escalation.' The statement was dictated to no one and received by the household with some scepticism.

A source close to the investigation — who is also Lucy — has suggested that the Bandit's approach was 'expected,' 'known,' and 'not a threat to monitored assets.' The source declined to elaborate on which assets are monitored, how the approach was known, or whether Lucy had prior contact with the visitor. A follow-up statement is expected by the weekend. It is expected to be equally uninformative.

stories.headline: Subcommittee Receives Bootprint Report; Immediately Motions to Expand Its Jurisdiction to Include Footwear; the Motion Passes; This Helps No One
body: The Ministry's Duck and Associated Phenomena Subcommittee convened at half past ten upon receiving the morning's bootprint report. Within six minutes it had passed an internal motion formally extending its mandate to include 'ambiguous footwear impressions within ten metres of a registered duck-bearing vehicle.' The motion was seconded by its own drafter, which the subcommittee's own procedural handbook does not permit, but the handbook is twelve years old and no one has re-read it.

The subcommittee has formally requested the bootprint's dimensions, bearing, and estimated stride length. It has not explained what it would do with these figures. Asked whether it was any closer to identifying the Duck Bandit, the subcommittee's chair confirmed that it had 'a number of promising angles.' The angles were not specified. The numeral 7 continues to occupy a separate file labelled, at this point, DUCK/7/FOOTWEAR/PENDING.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Statement has been issued. The statement stands. Further questions may be submitted in writing and will be assessed for relevance before being set aside.
Ellie: There is a shape on the drive that was not there yesterday. Ellie has sniffed it four times. Each time it has smelled like gravel. She is going to try once more.
Jersey: Jersey was on the warmest cushion from nine-fifteen to twelve-forty and considers this a productive morning by any reasonable measure.
founding_editor_note: That print is a size eleven. I'd start there. — D.

in_brief.sport: Thursday Deadlift Trials postponed; Christine was busy resolving a sub-jurisdictional goblin inheritance dispute, which is heavier.
in_brief.forecast: Overcast through evening; gravel undisturbed by mid-afternoon; the drive is being watched, though by whom remains the outstanding question.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Waits
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: A bootprint — left foot, partial, facing the passenger-side mirror — has been found at the edge of the drive. The Bandit was here between last light Wednesday and first light Thursday. Lucy did not bark and claims 'insufficient grounds for escalation,' which suggests prior knowledge of the visitor. The two ducks remain undisturbed at forty-seven degrees. Don's portrait notes the print is a size eleven. Day 4 should narrow the identity further: either a second physical token left by the Bandit (a small marked object, or a note), or a connection drawn between the size-eleven boot and someone known to have been near Harlan's Creek on the morning of the expedition — a named figure from the trail community, a familiar, or an unexpected party. Lucy's prior knowledge should be addressed or deepened.
